title: Netflix Unveils ‘Pride And Prejudice’ Series Trailer Teases Timeless Slow Burn Romance Between Jack Lowden’s Mr. Darcy & Emma Corrin’s Elizabeth Bennett
full_text: Skip to main content By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi Amy Poehler Leads Young Women Archaeologists Who Make An Important Discovery In Peacock’s ‘Dig’ Trailer Ryan Gosling & Zach Shields Duo Dead Man’s Bones Returns With New Song Plus Music Video Starring Rain Spencer And Noah Jupe ‘The Gilded Age’ Season 4 Release Schedule: When Do New Episodes Come Out? View All October 28, 2026 8:48am Add us as a Google Preferred Source UPDATED – Oct. 28, 8 a.m. – The full trailer for the Netflix limited series adaptation of Pride and Prejudice has arrived. The series, based on the book by Jane Austen , arrives on the streamer December 3. The clip opens with Emma Corrin’s Elizabeth Bennett and Freya Mavor’s Jane Bennett lying on a rooftop talking of the future. Related Stories Books Jane Austen Adaptations & Where They Are Streaming: ‘Sense And Sensibility’ To ‘Sanditon’ Books Georgia Oakley’s ‘Sense And Sensibility’ Cast Vs. Ang Lee’s 1995 Group: Who Plays Who? “One day, Jane, I shall be either a governess and a spinster, or a wife and a mother,” Corrin’s Lizzie says. “And then finally, we may talk about something else.” Jane and Elizabeth are two of the five Bennett sisters, parented by “a very animated mother” Mrs. Bennett (Olivia Colman) and father Mr. Bennett (Rufus Sewell), a man of few words. Elizabeth comes upon Mr. Darcy (Jack Lowden) skipping rocks on a lake, which curiously echoes George Mackay’s Mr. Edward Ferrars doing the same thing with Daisy Edgar Jones’ Elinor Dashwood in Georgia Oakley’s new film adaptation of Jane Austen’s Sense and Sensibility , which arrived in theaters earlier this month. Watch on Deadline Fiona Shaw as Lady Catherine de Bourgh in Netflix’s ‘Pride and Prejudice’ Another crossover between the two new adaptation projects is actress Fiona Shaw, who will portray Lady Catherine de Bourgh in the Netflix series. She can be spotted dressed in black in the back of a carriage. “It is a truth universally acknowledged that a single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife,” Colman says later on. Viewers also get glimpses at Rhea Norwood’s Lydia Bennett, Hopey Parish’s Mary Bennett and Hollie Avery’s Mary Bennett, Louis Partridge’s Mr. George Wickham, Jamie Demetriou’s Mr. Collins and more. The clip ends with Colman questioning why Sewell’s Mr. Bennett, who hasn’t spoken a word in the entire trailer, must make everything so dramatic. PREVIOUS, Feb. 24: The first teaser trailer for Netflix’s Pride & Prejudice series, based on Jane Austen’s classic novel, is here. The clip features Elizabeth Bennet (Emma Corrin) and Mr. Darcy (Jack Lowden). The six-part series will be a faithful, classic adaptation of the novel, written by Dolly Alderton ( Everything I Know About Love, Good Material ) and directed by Euros Lyn ( Heartstopper ). Alongside Corrin ( Nosferatu, Black Mirror ) and Lowden ( Slow Horses, Benediction ), Olivia Colman ( The Favourite, The Crown ) will be Mrs. Bennet, Rufus Sewell ( The Diplomat, Scoop ) will be Mr. Bennet, Freya Mavor ( Industry, La Dame Dans L’Auto ) will be Jane Bennet, Jamie Demetriou ( Stath Lets Flats, Barbie ) will be Mr. Collins and Daryl McCormack ( Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery; Good Luck to You, Leo Grande ) will be Mr. Bingley. Rhea Norwood ( Heartstopper ) will play Lydia Bennett, Hopey Parish and Hollie Avery will play Mary and Kitty Bennett, Siena Kelly will play Caroline Bingley, and Fiona Shaw ( Bad Sisters , Harry Potter ) will play Lady Catherine de Bourgh. When the full cast was revealed during production, writer and executive producer Alderton said: “‘Once in a generation, a group of people get to retell this wonderful story and I feel very lucky that I get to be a part of it. Jane Austen’s Pride and Prejudice is the blueprint for romantic comedy – it has been a joy to delve back into its pages to find both familiar and fresh ways of bringing this beloved book to life. With Euros Lyn directing our stellar cast, I am so excited to reintroduce these hilarious and complicated characters to those who count Pride and Prejudice as their favourite book, and those who are yet to meet their Lizzie and Mr. Darcy.” Other executive producers include Laura Lankester, Will Johnston and Louise Mutter for Lookout Point, as well as Alderton and Lyn. Corrin is also an executive producer, marking their debut in the role. Austen’s beloved novels have enraptured generations for over 200 years. Her most famous and widely-read novel, Pride and Prejudice has inspired countless writers and filmmakers with its iconic characters, sharp social commentary and timeless love story. In the UK last week, the teaser played on the big screen ahead of Emerald Fennell’s Wuthering Heights starring Margot Robbie and Jacob Elordi. Austen’s Sense and Sensibility will get a new adaptation in film form later this year as well from Focus Features starring Daisy Edgar-Jones as Elinor Dashwood, Esmé Creed-Miles as Marianne Dashwood, Catríona Balfe as Mrs. Dashwood and more. The 1995 film version of Sense and Sensibility starred Kate Winslet, Emma Thompson, Alan Rickman, Hugh Grant and more.

title: Free IP and Fresh Eyes: How Hollywood Is Reinventing the Classics
full_text: × Skip to main content East of Eden, A Tale of Two Cities, Sense and Sensibility photo illustration THR Staff/Nicholas Brawley Some stories refuse to stay on the page. The Hollywood Reporter’ s Beyond the Book column explores what happens when books make the leap to screen and beyond — unpacking what stayed, changed, how it was done and why it matters with the creatives who made it. *** East of Eden showrunner Zoe Kazan has had her eye on adapting John Steinbeck’s family saga since she first read it at 15. “Somebody has to put the thing on screen that I see in my head,” she told The Hollywood Reporter . And after “a good 20 years” of carrying that feeling, the opportunity to translate the story to screen finally came to fruition, with Kazan’s vision unfurling as an eight-episode Netflix limited series. Related Stories TV 'Transplant' Creator Joseph Kay Sets Overall Deal at Netflix TV 'Nobody Wants This' Star Condemns Adam Brody's Gaza "Genocide" Comments Hollywood has never been shy about mining the classics, with Pride and Prejudice , To Kill a Mockingbird and Little Women among the staples of film and TV’s page-to-screen catalog. This year, Kazan’s dip into the classic canon is joined by the likes of Christopher Nolan, who has taken on Homer’s The Odyssey , Emerald Fennell’s adaptation of Emily Brontë’s Wuthering Heights , and new versions of Jane Austen’s Sense and Sensibility and Charles Dickens’ A Tale of Two Cities . Steinbeck, Austen and Dickens come with name recognition, a built-in audience and, as Sense and Sensibility screenwriter Diana Reid puts it, “free IP.” But the prestige and name recognition only get a project so far with audiences desperate for something fresh. This year, the writers behind Netflix’s East of Eden , Focus Features ’ Sense and Sensibility and MGM+ ’s A Tale of Two Cities used that audience demand to do something different: leave the novels’ worlds intact and rebuild the people inside them. For Kazan, that meant re-reading Steinbeck’s Cathy. For Daniel West, it was giving Dickens’ Lucie a pulse. Reid let the Dashwood sisters Marianne and Elinor each grow into a bit of the other. And while a famous novel might spark initial curiosity, it offers no inherent road map once development begins. So rather than reimagining these books through a modern lens, each writer chose to lean into the ways the stories already transcend time. “You don’t need to spoon-feed the audience the modernity of it,” West says. Why a Classic Novel Already Has Appeal Esmé Creed-Miles stars as Marianne Dashwood and Daisy Edgar-Jones as Elinor Dashwood in Sense and Sensibility. Courtesy of Focus Features Reid is the first to admit the commercial logic of adapting a classic. “I think they are classic for a reason,” she says. But the appeal runs deeper. In an era of surface-level connection, she argues, audiences crave something that feels substantial. “There’s nothing more satisfying as an audience than encountering someone who’s superficially very different from you — they live in another time, they have different values and customs, they dress in a bizarre way — and then realizing that emotionally you have the same inner life.” She also knows she won’t be the last to take on Austen. “It’s nice to be part of such a big catalog. On one hand it’s an honor, and on the other it takes pressure off, because it’ll be one of many. It doesn’t need to be definitive.” West’s pitch for A Tale of Two Cities , a four-part series that premiered on MGM+ last month, started with what he calls a “unicorn”: a book with a huge cultural footprint that, by his account, hadn’t had a major screen adaptation in nearly 40 years. He and star and executive producer Kit Harington had been talking about adapting Dickens’ 1859 novel for roughly a decade, noting that there “hasn’t really been a seminal TV or film adaptation” of the story. “It was done quite a lot in the first half of the 20th century, but then it petered out. So a large part of the draw was the opportunity: There was this huge built-in audience that already knew the book, or at least knew of it,” he says. “The story itself is incredibly timely,” he adds. “It’s about a disenfranchised, broken society that is pushing back and reaching a crisis point. Within that, there’s a very personal, intimate love story.” Kazan has a personal tie to East of Eden — her grandfather, Elia Kazan, directed the 1955 film — but part of her motivation for making a series was to tell more of the novel than that film did. Though Steinbeck’s book was published in 1952, she says, “there’s this beautiful continuum between us and the past,” which is part of what makes revisiting a classic so appealing. Looking backward and forward at the same time, she adds, “is a profound part of what makes us human.” “It’s the opposite of AI. It’s not regurgitation, not spitting back up what we’ve already digested,” she says. “It’s why we should read these books. They’re like a bow shot across time from one human to another.” Rethinking the Novels’ Protagonists Mirren Mack as Lucie Manette in A Tale of Two Cities . Marcell Piti/Federation Studios/MGM+ Still, none of the three writers treated an established title as a safety net. Instead, their adaptations declined to modernize the novel’s setting and embraced finding new ways into the protagonists. While developing A Tale of Two Cities , West and his producers considered a contemporary reimagining early on before dropping it. “The issues these characters are dealing with, the injustice and the way it bleeds into vengeance and cruelty, already feel very 2026,” he says. What he changed instead was characterization. In Dickens’ novel, heroine Lucie Manette is “prone to a lot of weeping” and “quite a lot of fainting,” West says. “She’s not the most compelling heroine in large passages of it. So we made some fundamental changes. We made her much more intentional.” He wanted Lucie to be “the central pivot of the entire story” and “the investigative force” of the opening episodes, pushing against the walls of “buttoned-up Georgian London.” “That was a fairly big modernization from the book,” he says. Of Mirren Mack, who plays Lucie in the series, he adds: “Lucie is the central component of the whole thing, the sun at the center of the solar system, and then an actor arrives who delivers all of that and more and elevates it through her own interpretation.” He also replaced Jarvis Lorry and Miss Pross — who he felt were “serving a similar purpose” and were too “big and colorful” for the series’ taut, volatile tone — with a new character, Hester (Sharon Duncan-Brewster). “She isn’t a proxy father figure to Lucie. She’s an inherited family member, almost an inherited stepmother. … As the story goes on, they discover that they mean a lot to each other and are more than just inherited relations. They really are family, but they come to that on their own terms. That gives them a larger emotional distance to travel.” Thérèse Defarge (Roxane Duran) marks another departure. “We wanted to see somebody become, for want of a less anachronistic word, radicalized,” West says. “She starts as part of her community. She has a warmth and generosity. Because of what happens to her within the story, we see that crack begin to metastasize into something really sinister and ugly, and by the end, murderous. When we meet her in episode one, she’s a completely different person from what we see at the very end of the show.” From left: François Civil as Charles Darnay and Kit Harington as Sydney Carton in A Tale of Two Cities . Marcell Piti/Federation Studios/MGM+ Dickens’ book centers on a couple, but West wanted to “intensify that” and “twist it slightly into much more of a triangle and make it more live and more complex” between Sydney Carton (Harington), Lucie (Mack) and Charles Darnay (François Civil). “That way we don’t really know which way Lucie is going to go until she does, toward the back end of the story. I also wanted both men to be equally attractive, equally intriguing and volatile, each speaking to a different side of her, so we really feel the pull, the tension and the dilemma she’s wrestling with.” Kazan’s re-reading centered on Cathy Ames ( Florence Pugh ), the character who first hooked her in Steinbeck’s story. Writing the series, which released on Netflix on Oct. 1, she realized something she hadn’t anticipated: Cathy “is almost always telling the truth.” A fresh perspective also helped Kazan see the story as a love story between brothers Adam (Christopher Abbott) and Charles (Mike Faist), one that Cathy interrupts. “By watching Chris and Mike interact, I understood how much these characters loved each other,” she says. Respecting the Literary Blueprint — and Knowing When to Change It Creative liberties, the writers insist, aren’t changes for the sake of it. Reid describes her approach as “respect rather than reverence.” Her biggest liberty is a duel between Herbert Nordrum’s Colonel Brandon and Frank Dillane’s John Willoughby, which Austen mentions but keeps offstage. “Hearing about things secondhand in a novel is not so confusing, but on screen, hearing a character describe it isn’t very interesting,” she says. “You need to see it to reveal the drama.” Austen’s voice also served as a guide for balancing drama with wit. “When I read the book, I made a note of the lines that made me laugh, and a lot of those ended up verbatim in the film. Jane Austen’s just really funny,” Reid says. Cathy “is almost always telling the truth,“ Kazan says. Kirsty Griffin/Netflix Kazan’s challenge was the opposite: too much book. She was only interested in adapting it as a series because “the book is simply too big,” and even with seven episodes, “half is not in our series.” For A Tale of Two Cities , West’s key structural decision was genre. “I always wanted it to be a thriller: a very taut, limited story,” he explains. “Four episodes felt like the perfect length to keep the pace and stakes up, and to never let any of the characters settle. I really wanted to make sure that all the characters, whether they’re in London or Paris or moving between the two, are always in a state of agitation. Their feet are never quite on solid ground, so we feel the jeopardy and the volatility of their world.” Why We Keep Going Back Left to right: Mike Faist, Christopher Abbott and Florence Pugh in Netflix‘s East of Eden. Courtesy of Netflix Asked why classics keep returning, each offers their own perspective. West points to archetypes and longevity. A Tale of Two Cities , he says, “is the archetypal sacrificial story,” with “strong parallels in that act of sacrifice to the Bible and all the stories that form the basis of our narratives and our emotional map of the world.” Classics “still feel timeless, and they still feel as resonant today,” West adds. “The key thing for us as creatives is to find a new way of telling those classic stories, an angle and something new to say about them. That doesn’t mean reinventing the wheel. It just means giving yourself the license to look at them with fresh eyes.” Reid returns to the idea that classics are “classics for a reason.” She explains that “when an audience doesn’t feel patronized” and an adaptation allows “the classic to exist in its own time, that makes for incredibly powerful viewing.” Kazan sees adaptations as a way to lower the barrier for new readers. “One thing these adaptations can do is make a general audience feel they have access to East of Eden , The Odyssey , Wuthering Heights .” While they have differing ideas about what keeps the classics coming back, all three writers share the same hope: that viewers will pick up the book. Classics haven’t disappeared from school reading lists, but students are reportedly reading significantly fewer full-length books than in past decades. “As long as we don’t ban and burn these books, everybody will continue to have access to them,” Kazan says. “There are so many books I came to as an adult that changed my life, and if I’d read them in high school, I wouldn’t have cared or understood. The most important thing is to let kids feel they can have pleasure in reading.” There’s already evidence that these adaptations are sending people back to the page. Since the series’ Oct. 1 debut, sales of East of Eden have risen nearly 200 percent across all formats, according to publisher Penguin Classics. The novel also hit No. 1 on Amazon’s bestsellers list — 74 years after it was published. The Economist reports that U.S. sales of The Odyssey have quadrupled this year, while Wuthering Heights topped Britain’s bestseller list. “Anything that can nudge people back toward bookshops and toward discovering those works again can only be a good thing,” West says. “The reason the work of classic storytellers like Dickens, Shakespeare and Austen still resonates is that they’re saying something about the human condition, about what we’re all struggling with, yearning for and reaching for.” “It would be amazing if people went back to the book,” Reid says. If Sense and Sensibility “could make Austen and the classics feel less intimidating, and encourage people to see themselves in it and find emotional truth in a story they thought was too remote, that would be amazing!” “It would be amazing if people went back to the book,” Sense and Sensibility screenwriter Reid says. title: Fox News Ratings Sink a Staggering 27% in October, but It Still Has Much a Larger Audience Than CNN or MS NOW
full_text: × Oct 28, 2026 8:10am PT Fox News Ratings Sink a Staggering 27% in October, but It Still Has Much a Larger Audience Than CNN or MS NOW By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest Fox News Ratings Sink a Staggering 27% in October, but It Still Has Much a Larger Audience Than CNN or MS NOW 14 minutes ago Elmo Is Going as Meryl Streep’s Evil Fashion Editor Miranda Priestly for Halloween This Year 18 hours ago Trump Says ‘Artificial Intelligence’ Is ‘a Very Bad and Inaccurate Name,’ and That He Wants to Officially Ban the Term ‘AI’ 21 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Fox News In the lead-up to the 2026 midterm elections, Fox News lost more than a quarter of its overall viewing audience in the month of October, according to new data. That said, the network remains the most-watched news outlet on cable, well ahead of rivals CNN and MS NOW . For October 2026, Fox News is on track to post its lowest-rated month in total-day viewers since December 2023, according to preliminary figures from Nielsen, first reported by Status. FNC averaged 1.1 million total viewers for the month, down 27%, and 98,000 viewers in the key 25-54 demographic coveted by advertisers, a drop of 32%. Related Stories Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’ The ratings decline comes amid a continuation of the drop-off in TV viewers overall — but Fox News has been losing viewers at a double-digit clip as CNN and MS NOW have been slightly up in recent months. As Variety has reported, Fox News on many nights draws a bigger live audience than one or more broadcast TV networks. But its viewership is steadily eroding: In the third quarter of 2026, Fox News saw total-day viewership decline 16%, and viewership in the 25-54 demo fall 24%. Both CNN and MS NOW saw small gains in overall audience for Q3. In primetime, Fox News averaged about 2 million total viewers (down 28% year over year) in October, with viewers in the 25-54 demo falling 36% to 183,000, according to the Nielsen data. “Fox & Friends” had its second consecutive month below 1 million total viewers and under 100,000 in the key demo, with October representing its lowest overall viewers since July 2015 (and its lowest in the 25-54 demographic since June 2001). Meanwhile, progressive rival MS NOW saw its daytime audience rise 16% to 588,000 total viewers in October, and CNN viewership was up 3% to 402,000 viewers over the same timeframe, according to the preliminary Nielsen figures. Variety has reached out to Fox News for comment. Some observers detect a worrisome sign in Fox News’ ratings decline that conservatives are tuning out at rates faster than CNN or MS NOW as the fight for control of the Senate and House of Representatives will be up for grabs on Election Day next week, Nov. 3. President Donald Trump — whose feelings about Fox News historically run hot and cold — recently complained that the network has not been backing Republicans strongly enough. “Fox spends more time defending Dumocrats, and putting on their views versus their Republican opponent, than at any time in the History of FoxNews,” Trump wrote in an Oct. 19 post on Truth Social. “It’s ridiculous! title: TikTok Wants to Help Its Users Find Their Next Must Eat
full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 28, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Photo Illustration by Justin Sullivan/Getty Images TikTok ‘s U.S. joint venture is leaning hard into the food creator community, launching a new product called Must Eat that is meant to boost food creators, as well as restaurants, all in service of helping its users find that next must visit place to grab a bite. The company officially rolled out Must Eat at a reception held at Undercote in New York City Tuesday evening, with Adam Presser, the CEO of TikTok’s U.S. business, hosting food creators in the lounge. “The first time that I came across FoodTok was actually before I joined the company, it was in the pandemic,” Presser told the attendees. “I came across the feta cheese pasta trend … So we were lucky enough to be able to get a block of feta cheese at that time, and we made the recipe, and it was incredible. And it was that first experience of being able to be watching videos, consuming content, and then translating that into real life experiences. And that journey has only continued on TikTok. “The ‘lunch in my city’ trend has really driven a lot of momentum,” he continued. “I know some of the creators here have made content around that trend. I have tried it out, it’s fantastic. And over the last several years, we’ve just seen more and more people have this experience of discovering something on the platform and driving their in-real-life experience. I saw a stat last year: More than 27 million Americans went to an independent restaurant, cafe, or store in the U.S. that they had discovered for the first time on TikTok.” So, Must Eat. The product is launching in New York, Los Angeles and the Bay Area, highlighting places in two categories: “Everyday Eats” and “Elevated Dining” featuring restaurants that have connected with TikTok food creators. TikTok also partnered with OpenTable to enable reservations at selected locations. The product, an expansion of “Must GO” (focused on travel), is an example of how TikTok U.S. is trying to carve its own path forward, now 10 months or so into its new ownership structure. For Presser, it is also a chance to bring his own imprint onto one of the biggest creator platforms in the country. “I am an L.A. native, and probably like most people that grew up in L.A., I had dreams of working in entertainment, but any hope of working in front of the camera were quickly dashed — I think it was around the eighth grade play. I was assigned the role of lighting director,” he quipped Tuesday, noting that he went on to work in the music industry and later as an executive at Warner Bros. Discovery before joining TikTok some four and a half years ago. “It was the first time that I really had the experience of realizing that you didn’t have to be at the top of the charts or on the big screen to be a star,” he said. “That it could be anybody with a voice, and a phone, and a vision, a creative perspective, and a platform like TikTok that could bring people’s voices to the world and have people discover the incredible, talented people that had something to say. So it is truly a dream come true.” THR

title: Sundance Sets Legacy Screenings Including Films by Christopher Nolan, Justin Lin and Alfonso Cuarón
full_text: × Skip to main content By Chris Gardner Plus Icon Chris Gardner chrissgardner Follow Sign Up View All October 28, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source A still from Justin Lin's 'Better Luck Tomorrow.' Courtesy of Sundance Institute As Sundance prepares to write a new legacy in Boulder, Colorado in 2027 and beyond, the film festival is bringing some hits from its past to the new home. Sundance Institute today revealed the lineup for the Legacy program for next year’s festival, and it includes works by filmmakers including Christopher Nolan, Alfonso Cuarón , Justin Lin , Stacy Peralta, Julie Taymor, Barbara Hammer, Patricia Cardoso and Tom Kalin. While old will be new again, there’s also something fresh for the lineup once known as From the Collection: Letterboxd joins as a co-presenter of the Legacy program with additional details for onsite activations to come. Related Stories Movies Alfonso Cuarón Reflects on Making 'Harry Potter': "Two of the Most Beautiful Years of My Life" 'Awards Chatter' Podcast John Leguizamo on 'The Odyssey,' Non-Traditional Casting and Being Uninvited From 'Spider-Man: Homecoming' Plucked for the Legacy program — curated as a home to showcase “groundbreaking independent cinema including archival and restoration screenings of fiction and nonfiction works as well as special events” — will feature brand-new restorations of the 2002 Sundance version of Lin’s Better Luck Tomorrow , a digital 4K restoration of Peralta’s Dogtown and Z-Boys , a 35th anniversary screening of Taymor’s Fool’s Fire , Hammer’s Nitrate Kisses , a 25th anniversary screening of Cardoso’s Real Women Have Curves, a star making turn for America Ferrera, a 35th anniversary screening of Kalin’s Swoon , and a 25th anniversary screening of a 4K restoration of Cuarón’s Y tu mamá también, a star making turn for Diego Luna and Gael Garcia Bernal. (Top left to right): Better Luck Tomorrow and Dogtown and Z-Boys ; (middle left to right): Fool’s Fire, Nitrate Kisses and Real Women Have Curves ; (bottom left to right): Swoon and Y tu mamá también . Legacy screenings will include director appearances and select cast members in attendance. Courtesy of Sundance Institute Sundance has also set a special two-part session on the final weekend of the festival dubbed “ Sundance Film Festival presents: Cinema Interruptus featuring Memento .” It will feature a 4K restoration and communal discussion for Nolan’s 2000 effort, Memento, starring Guy Pearce, Carrie-Anne Moss and Joe Pantoliano. “We’re excited to kick off the festival season in earnest with this first 2027 Sundance Film Festival announcement, revealing some of our Legacy programming,” explained Eugene Hernandez, who serves as director of the Sundance Film Festival and public programming. “Each year we honor the legacy of our founder Robert Redford and the history of the Sundance Film Festival by looking back at just a few of the films and filmmakers who have shaped our history. Our first festival in our new home in Boulder, Colorado will bring change, but as we evolve, we’ll keep at our core what we celebrate: our rich history.” Added Kim Yutani, director of programming: “Revisiting and becoming newly acquainted with films from our previous lineups in a theatrical setting, in community, and with some of the talent behind the films is a rare treat — even more so when these projects have been restored. We’re really looking forward to welcoming back these artists and know that audiences will enjoy the opportunity to complement the new films we will soon be announcing with these classics.” The Sundance Film Festival will take place in Boulder from Jan. 21–31. Additional Legacy programming will be announced in the coming weeks. THR

title: Environmental Media Association and Its Awards Show to Become Part of Nonprofit United by Nature
full_text: × Skip to main content By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All October 28, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source The 2025 Environmental Media Awards Gala. Amy Sussman/Getty Images for The Environmental Media Association It’s a new era for the Environmental Media Association, as the Hollywood sustainability group is becoming a part of nonprofit United by Nature. EMA has been active in the industry for nearly 40 years, creating conversation through educational initiatives, industry partnerships and events like the Impact Summit and its signature EMA Awards Gala. United by Nature — an organization focused on building the next generation of America’s conservation movement — plans to build upon these programs and relationships, as well as host the first United by Nature Awards in April 2027 to coincide with Earth Month. Related Stories News 'The Wild Robot,' 'The Daily Show' Among Winners at Environmental Media Awards News Stars Talk L.A Wildfires, Home Rebuilds and What to Do With Your Tesla at EMA Impact Summit “Environmental progress requires a bigger coalition that’s more reflective of communities across America,” Benji Backer, founder and CEO of United by Nature, said in a statement. “EMA proved how powerful storytelling can shape culture, unite people and drive meaningful outcomes for nature. Together, we’re building upon that impact by reaching new audiences and inviting people of all backgrounds to protect the outdoors they love.” Debbie Levin, the former CEO of EMA who will now serve as chief visionary officer of United by Nature, said, “EMA has always believed in the extraordinary power of entertainment and storytelling to inspire environmental action. For more than three decades, we’ve worked alongside the entertainment community to make sustainability part of the cultural conversation. We’re proud of the legacy we’ve built, and we’re excited to work with United by Nature to reach new audiences and continue making sustainability more accessible and engaging.” United by Nature’s inaugural takeover of the awards event will continue to celebrate the entertainment industry’s environmental leadership, while also expanding to recognize the individuals and organizations across music, sports, podcasts and universities that inspire positive change. Past EMA honorees include Billie Eilish, Michael Bloomberg, Jane Fonda, Ted Turner, Natalie Portman, Matt Damon and Laura Dern. The EMA Green Seal will also become the United by Nature Green Seal, which recognizes industries that take meaningful steps to reduce their environmental footprint. Wildwood , the animated fantasy film from Laika Studios, is the first movie to be awarded the United by Nature Green Seal; the movie joins nearly 3,000 other productions recognized for their sustainability efforts. title: Sundance 2027 In Boulder Unveils Legacy Lineup With ‘Better Luck Tomorrow’, ‘Memento’, ‘Y Tu Mamá También’ & More
full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony How ‘Klara And The Sun’ Got Blotted Out At The Box Office ‘Divine Rivals’: Feature Take Of Rebecca Ross Fantasy Romance Bestseller Heads To Disney Searchlight Pictures Marketing EVP Michelle Hooper Leaving Studio View All October 28, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Sundance Film Festival 2027 has announced its first lineup for the inaugural Boulder, Colorado edition with the The Legacy Program, formerly known as From the Collection, which includes archival and restored screenings of indie classics that launched at the fest. Cinephile social platform, Letterboxd, is a co-presenter of the Legacy program, and there will be forthcoming details for onsite activations at the Boulder cinema event which takes place Jan. 21-31. The Legacy portion of Sundance will occur during the fest’s second half from Tuesday, Jan. 27-Sunday, Jan. 31. Related Stories Acquisitions Jenna Ortega, Natalie Portman MRC Comedy 'The Gallerist' Heads To Roadside Attractions & Vertical In U.S. Deal Festivals Sundance Film Festival Boulder Expanding Competition Lineup & Making Big Cinema Upgrades For 2027 Event There will still be an online portion of the festival, which will run from Thursday, Jan. 28-Sunday, Jan. 31. The Legacy lineup includes the 2002 Sundance Film Festival version of Better Luck Tomorrow (Justin Lin); a digital 4K restoration of Dogtown and Z-Boys (Stacy Peralta); a 35th anniversary screening of Fool’s Fire (Julie Taymor); Nitrate Kisses (Barbara Hammer), which premiered in the U.S. at the Festival 35 years ago and whose director is at the center of Brydie O’Connor’s 2026 Sundance Film Festival documentary Barbara Forever ; a 25th anniversary screening of Real Women Have Curves (Patricia Cardoso); a 35th anniversary screening of Swoon (Tom Kalin); and a 25th anniversary screening of a 4K restoration of Y tu mamá también (Alfonso Cuarón). Watch on Deadline The Legacy program will also include a two-part session on the final weekend of the Festival called “Sundance Film Festival presents: Cinema Interruptus featuring Memento ” (Christopher Nolan), featuring a 4K restoration and discussion. Legacy screenings will include director appearances and select cast members in attendance, Next reps the 30th anniversary of Sundance Institute and the UCLA Film & Television Archive. Together they established a film preservation initiative, the Sundance Institute Collection at UCLA, to ensure the long-term preservation of independent film. The Collection currently holds material from over 1,000 titles and has participated in restorations of Hoop Dreams , River of Grass , Mysterious Skin , Doom Generation , Just Another Girl on the IRT , High Art , Go Fish , Three Seasons , Paris Is Burning , Superstar , Unzipped , The Hours and Times , SLAM , and, this year, Better Luck Tomorrow and Swoon . “We’re excited to kick off the Festival season in earnest with this first 2027 Sundance Film Festival announcement, revealing some of our Legacy programming,” said Eugene Hernandez, Director, Sundance Film Festival and Public Programming. “Each year we honor the legacy of our founder Robert Redford and the history of the Sundance Film Festival by looking back at just a few of the films and filmmakers who have shaped our history. Our first festival in our new home in Boulder, Colorado will bring change, but as we evolve, we’ll keep at our core what we celebrate: our rich history. Sundance will always uplift independent voices, and our Legacy slate is a beautiful example of that. We are also pleased to announce Letterboxd’s co-partnership for the Legacy category — it’s great to collaborate with organizations that build momentum and excitement for a culture of cinematic discovery, and we look forward to having them at the Festival with us in January.” “Revisiting and becoming newly acquainted with films from our previous lineups in a theatrical setting, in community, and with some of the talent behind the films is a rare treat — even more so when these projects have been restored,” said Kim Yutani, Director of Programming, Sundance Film Festival. “We’re really looking forward to welcoming back these artists and know that audiences will enjoy the opportunity to complement the new films we will soon be announcing with these classics.” “Our Legacy programming at the Sundance Film Festival grew out of a partnership with the UCLA Film & Television Archive and its continued growth is running in parallel to the incredible moment repertory cinema is having across the country right now,” said John Nein, Sundance Film Festival Senior Programmer and Director of Strategic Initiatives. “This program offers a space for brand-new restorations of classic independent films to be discovered or rediscovered by audiences as the creative teams behind these films reunite — it’s an exciting way of celebrating what these artists have brought to independent storytelling.” Below are descriptions of the Legacy lineup: 25th Anniversary of Better Luck Tomorrow / U.S.A. (Director, Screenwriter, and Producer: Justin Lin, Screenwriters: Ernesto Foronda, Fabian Marquez, Producers: Julie Asato, Ernesto Foronda) — To escape the crushing pressure of academic perfection, a group of high-achieving teens lead a secret, thrill-seeking double life of petty crime that quickly spins out of control. Cast: Karin Anna Cheung, John Cho, Roger Fan, Sung Kang, Parry Shen, Jason Tobin. Fiction. Better Luck Tomorrow premiered at the 2002 Sundance Film Festival as part of the U.S. Dramatic Competition. It was subsequently released with small changes in the edit. The original 2002 Sundance Film Festival cut of Better Luck Tomorrow was restored by the UCLA Film & Television Archive in collaboration with Sundance Institute and Perfect Storm Entertainment, with funding provided by Chris Quintos Cathcart, co-CEO of Unapologetic Projects. The 4K restoration utilized the original 35 mm camera negatives, 35 mm Sundance Film Festival print, and DA-88 sound materials and was supervised by filmmaker Justin Lin at Resillion and Deluxe Audio Services. Additional lab services by Roundabout Entertainment, Inc. The release version has also been restored and archived. Special thanks to Paramount Pictures for permission to screen the film. 25th Anniversary of Dogtown and Z-Boys / U.S.A (Director and Screenwriter: Stacy Peralta, Screenwriter: Craig Stecyk, Producer: Agi Orsi) — The Z-Boys: outcast surf rats from the run-down Dogtown neighborhood in Venice, California, who revolutionized skateboarding with their innovative style and attitude. The documentary is an exploration of the birth of a cultural phenomenon, narrated by Sean Penn and featuring old-school skating footage, a blistering soundtrack, and interviews with Tony Alva, Jay Adams, and Tony Hawk. Dogtown and Z-Boys premiered at the 2001 Sundance Film Festival as part of the U.S. Documentary Competition and won the Audience Award: Documentary and Directing Award: Documentary. 2027 marks the 25th anniversary of its theatrical release. The 4K digital restoration was undertaken from the original 35 mm elements by Sony Pictures Classics. The restoration was approved by the filmmakers. 35th Anniversary of Fool’s Fire / U.S.A. (Director, Screenwriter, and Producer: Julie Taymor, Producer: Kerry Orent) — A captured dwarf, Hopfrog, is forced to become jester to a tyrannical king. But when the King is gifted with another little person, whom the king debases and shames, Hopfrog plots a terrible revenge. Based on the story “Hop-Frog” by Edgar Allan Poe. Cast: Michael J. Anderson, Tom Hewitt, Mireille Mossé. Fiction. Fool’s Fire premiered at the 1992 Sundance Film Festival as part of the U.S. Dramatic Competition. This new restoration was created by the nonprofit IndieCollect in collaboration with Julie Taymor and with support from the Golden Globe Foundation, using a 6.5K scan of the original 35 mm negative and a soundtrack restored by Endpoint Audio Labs from the optical track negative. Featuring an extended conversation with Julie Taymor and clips from The Making of Fool’s Fire , exploring the film’s artistry and cutting-edge use of high definition. Nitrate Kisses / U.S.A. (Director: Barbara Hammer) — A portrait of queer sexuality that weaves striking images of four lesbian and gay couples with archival footage, interviews, sexual imagery, and queer cinema dating back to the 1930s to unearth forbidden and long-invisible histories. Documentary. Nitrate Kisses had its U.S. premiere at the 1993 Sundance Film Festival as part of the U.S. Documentary Competition. Nitrate Kisses was preserved by the Academy Film Archive. The original 16 mm A/B-rolls were scanned at 4K and restored by BB Optics. The mono mix was digitized from the original 16 mm mag track. The restoration was funded by Frameline and supervised by The Estate of Barbara Hammer and Brydie O’Connor. The 25th Anniversary of Real Women Have Curves / U.S.A. (Director: Patricia Cardoso, Screenwriters: George LaVoo, Josefina López, Producers: George Lavoo, Effie Brown) — Ana, a first-generation Mexican American teenager, fights for her independence and her curves in a war of wills with her mother. Based on the play by Josefina López. Cast: America Ferrera, George Lopez, Ingrid Oliu, Lupe Ontiveros, Brian Sites. Real Women Have Curves premiered at the 2002 Sundance Film Festival as part of the U.S. Dramatic Competition and took home the Audience Award: Dramatic and the Special Jury Prize for Acting for America Ferrera and Lupe Ontiveros. Supervised by director Patricia Cardoso and director of photography Jim Denault, this new 4K restoration was undertaken by Criterion in collaboration with Warner Bros. Pictures, Sundance Institute, and the Academy Film Archive from the 35 mm original camera negative. The 35th Anniversary of Swoon / U.S.A. (Director and Screenwriter: Tom Kalin, Producers: Christine Vachon) — The true story of Nathan Leopold and Richard Loeb, who kidnapped and brutally murdered 14-year-old Bobby Franks in Chicago in 1924. The revelation that these wealthy Jewish college students had a sexual relationship scandalized the nation. After their arrest and trial, they were sentenced to life plus 99 years. Cast: Craig Chester, Michael Kirby, John A. Mudd, Daniel Schlachet, Natalie Stanford, Michael Stumm, Ron Vawter. Swoon premiered at the 1992 Sundance Film Festival as part of the U.S. Dramatic Competition and took home the Excellence in Cinematography Award: Dramatic. Swoon was restored by the Academy Film Archive and UCLA Film & Television Archive in collaboration with Frameline, Strand Releasing, and Sundance Institute in 4K from the original 16 mm A/B camera negatives, 35 mm interpositive, 35 mm dupe negative, and 35 mm magnetic track. The restoration was supervised by Tom Kalin and Ellen Kuras at Roundabout Entertainment, Inc. and Deluxe Audio Services. Restoration funding was provided by the Academy Film Archive and UCLA Film & Television Archive with additional support from Frameline, Ellen Kuras, Strand Releasing, and Sundance Institute. The 25th Anniversary of Y tu mamá también / Mexico (Director, Screenwriter and Producer: Alfonso Cuarón, Screenwriter: Carlos Cuarón, Producer: Jorge Vergara) — After their girlfriends jet off for the summer, a pair of Mexico City teenagers become bewitched by an older Spanish woman they meet at a wedding. When she agrees to accompany them on a road trip, the three form an increasingly intense and sensual bond. Cast: Gael García Bernal, Diego Luna, Maribel Verdú. Y tu mamá también screened at the 2002 Sundance Film Festival as part of the Special Events category. Newly restored by Esperanto Films in 4K under the supervision of filmmaker Alfonso Cuarón and cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki. The feature is a Janus Films release. MEMENTO, Guy Pearce, 2000 LEGACY SPECIAL EVENTS Memento / U.S.A. (Director: Christopher Nolan) — A former insurance investigator who now suffers from anterograde amnesia uses notes and tattoos to hunt down his wife’s murderer. Fiction. Memento had its U.S. festival premiere at the 2001 Sundance Film Festival in the U.S. Dramatic Competition and it took home the Waldo Salt Screenwriting Award. Restored in 4K from original interpositive materials by Umbrella with approval from director Christopher Nolan. Cinema Interruptus is also part of our Offscreen program, to be announced in its entirety soon. As part of the screening, there will be Sundance Film Festival presents: Cinema Interruptus featuring Memento . A tradition first established by the late Roger Ebert, Cinema Interruptus is communal film criticism in two sessions. As Memento screens, participants can yell “Stop!” at any point to make a comment or ask a question, after which the film will resume. Critic and author Josh Larsen — who hosted Interruptus at the University of Colorado Boulder’s Conference on World Affairs from 2017 to 2024 — will moderate the discussion, with the goal of finishing the entire movie by the end of the second session. title: Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander & Rohan Campbell Set For Scout Taylor-Compton’s Horror Movie ‘Survive: The Game’; Filming Underway In Spain
full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Four ‘Star Trek’ Vets Reunite For Sci-Fi ‘Life 2.0’, OneTwoThree Media Launches AFM Sales; Brit Comedy With Stephen Fry, Jane Horrocks Also On Slate Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander & Rohan Campbell Set For Scout Taylor-Compton’s Horror Movie ‘Survive: The Game’; Filming Underway In Spain Tracee Ellis Ross, Lake Bell & Ken Leung Thriller ‘Blow The Horn’ Heads To AFM For Sales View All October 28, 2026 7:38am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander & Rohan Campbell Jonny Marlow, Slaven Vlasic, Alim Sabir EXCLUSIVE : Olivia Holt ( Heart Eyes ), Jaimie Alexander ( Thor ) and Rohan Campbell ( Halloween Ends ) have been set to lead Scout Taylor-Compton’s Survive: The Game , a horror movie currently filming entirely in Gipuzkoa, Spain, at Zinealdea Studios, and on location in Irún, Spain. The synopsis reads: “When a group of friends unearth an ancient board game inside a secluded cabin with a violent past, each roll of the dice brings a deadly fate to life, and the only way to survive is to finish the game.” Holt, who recently starred in horror Heart Eyes , will appear opposite Alexander, best known for her five-season run as Jane Doe on Blindspot and her recurring role as Lady Sif in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Campbell, who broke out opposite Jamie Lee Curtis in Halloween Ends and currently stars in Netflix’s Below , rounds out the lead cast. Related Stories Agencies Independent Creative Management Signs Serhat Metin News Tracee Ellis Ross, Lake Bell & Ken Leung Thriller 'Blow The Horn' Heads To AFM For Sales Taylor-Compton is directing from a script she wrote with Michael Kennedy ( Heart Eyes ). An actress-turned-filmmaker known for the Halloween franchise, she previously wrote and directed Road to Recovery and co-directed Last Chance Motel . Watch on Deadline The film is being produced by Randy Wayne and Talia Bella under their Rebellium Films banner, Tom O’Connell and Scout Taylor-Compton of Building Blocks Productions, and Amy Covell of Red Phoenix Productions. Executive producers include Leire Apellaniz of Sr. y Sra., Mark Albela, Michael Kennedy, and Dauntless Productions. The production sees the film as having franchise potential. “I’ve played the final girl. I spent years learning what it takes to survive a horror movie: the running, the screaming, the moment you finally turn around and fight,” said Taylor-Compton. “With Survive: The Game , I wanted to ask a different question. What if the thing chasing you isn’t outside the door? What if surviving means confronting the worst version of yourself first?” “This is the fourth film we’ve worked on with Scout, and the second she’s directing for Rebellium,” said producer Randy Wayne. “She’s a powerhouse with an extreme attention to detail and an unmatched drive. Audiences are going to meet antagonists they’ve never seen before – creative, scary, and inventive. We’re honored to help bring Survive: The Game to life with her.” Holt is repped by WME, Entertainment 360, and Yorn, Levine. Alexander is repped by Gersh, Berwick & Kovacik and Ginsburg Daniels Kallis. Campbell is repped by CAA, Sol22 and Webster Talent Management. Taylor-Compton is repped by Innovative Artists. title: Peter Medak, Director of ‘The Changeling’ and ‘The Krays,’ Dies at 88
full_text: × Oct 28, 2026 7:18am PT Peter Medak, Director of ‘The Changeling’ and ‘The Krays,’ Dies at 88 Medak also worked extensively in television, directing episodes of "Breaking Bad" and "The Wire." By Anna Tingley Plus Icon Anna Tingley Latest Peter Medak, Director of ‘The Changeling’ and ‘The Krays,’ Dies at 88 1 hour ago As NFL Expands Globally, Marriott Bonvoy Taps Cooper Kupp, Jerry Rice and More for City Travel Guides 20 hours ago Joy Behar Returns to ‘The View’ After Nearly a Month Away: ‘I Dislocated My Shoulder’ and the Pain Was ‘Worse Than Childbirth’ 24 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Peter Medak , the Hungarian-born director and actor best known for films including “ The Changeling ,” “ The Krays ” and “The Ruling Class” died Tuesday in Los Angeles. He was 88. Over a career spanning six decades, Medak directed 27 feature films, moving between psychological horror, black comedy and crime dramas. His 1980 supernatural thriller “The Changeling,” starring George C. Scott, won eight Genie Awards including best motion picture. He also directed the 1990 British gangster drama “The Krays,” for which he received the Evening Standard Award for best director. Related Stories Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’ Born in Budapest in 1937, Medak spent part of World War II in hiding with his family. Under Hungary’s Communist regime, his father was imprisoned and Medak was barred from attending school. He fled to England during the Hungarian Revolution of 1956 and began working in the British film industry, eventually serving as assistant director before moving to Hollywood. He made his feature directorial debut with 1968’s “Negatives,” starring Glenda Jackson. His 1972 satire “The Ruling Class,” starring Peter O’ Toole, competed for the Palme d’Or at Cannes and earned an Oscar nomination for Toole. Other credits include “A Day in the Death of Joe Egg,” “Let Him Have It” and the Gary Oldman-led “Romeo Is Bleeding.” Medak also worked extensively in television, directing episodes of “Homocide: Life on the Street,” “The Wire,” “Breaking Bad” and “House.” His 2018 documentary “The Ghost of Peter Sellars” revisited his troubled production of the 1970s comedy “Ghost in the Noonday Sun.” He is survived by his four children, Christopher, Joshua, Karen and Cornela, and five grandchildren. title: On Air Fest Sets Initial Talent Lineup for 10th Anniversary Edition in Brooklyn
full_text: × Skip to main content By Chris Gardner Plus Icon Chris Gardner chrissgardner Follow Sign Up View All October 28, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Megan Rapinoe, Dr. Sanjay Gupta, Audie Cornish, Ari Shapiro and Sam Sanders. Getty Images On Air Fest will soon be on air in Brooklyn, New York. The sound and storytelling festival mounted by On Air Presents has revealed the initial lineup of headliners and talent set to take the stage at venues including the Wythe Hotel and Arlo Williamsburg from Feb. 23-25, 2027, organized under a theme of “10 Years On…” to mark a milestone 10th anniversary. The first drop of names includes headliners Megan Rapinoe, Dr. Sanjay Gupta, Audie Cornish & Ari Shapiro, Dan Harris, Anthony Fantano, On the Media, One Song, World Café and more across live podcasts , conversations, performances, parties and events focused on the future of storytelling. There will be live recordings of Why Are You Like This with Megan Rapinoe , CNN’s Chasing Life with Dr. Sanjay Gupta , and 10 Percent Happier with Dan Harri s, CNN’s Engagement Party with Audie Cornish and Ari Shapiro , WNYC’s On The Media with Brooke Gladstone and Micah Loewinger, and WXPN’s World Café with Raina Douris. Also booked to make appearances are music critic Anthony Fantano, The Sam Sanders Show’s Sam Sanders, One Song hosts Diallo Riddle and Blake “LUXXURY” Robin, and Chameleon’s Josh Dean. Leon Neyfakh and Sayre Quevedo are set to discuss narrative podcasting in a conversation centered on Death of an Artist and Reaching Out , while actor and comedian Connor Ratliff will host a main stage. Kicking things off on Feb. 23 will be the Podcast Business Summit presented with Bloomberg at Wythe Hotel. Hosted by Bloomberg reporter Ashley Carman, the invite-only daytime gathering is expected to host leaders across media, technology, advertising, publishing and podcasting. Later that night, the Podcast Academy will present the Ambies, an awards show to honor excellence in podcasting at Arlo Williamsburg. Additional programming and talent names will be announced in coming weeks and months. Previous participants at On Air Fest have included Anderson Cooper, Malcolm Gladwell, Seth Meyers, Norah Jones, Wyclef Jean, Bon Iver’s Justin Vernon, Audie Cornish, Jad Abumrad, Terry Gross, Francis Ford Coppola, Ira Glass and more. title: ‘Transplant’ Creator Joseph Kay Sets Overall Deal at Netflix
full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 28, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Joseph Kay Courtesy of Netflix Netflix has signed an exclusive overall deal with Joseph Kay, the creator and showrunner of the medical drama Transplant , which landed on NBC stateside. As part of the deal, Kay will develop and write new TV series for Netflix in Canada, starting with an untitled new family drama. He most recently worked with Netflix as a consulting producer on North of North season 2, the Arctic-set comedy also on the CBC and set to return on Nov. 5. Also for Netflix, he co-executive produced the upcoming adaptation of Carley Fortune’s bestselling novel, This Summer Will Be Different. Transplant, which ran for four seasons, was a medical procedural about a Syrian refugee working as a doctor in a Toronto trauma unit. The drama centered on Dr. Bashir “Bash” Hamed (Hamza Haq, Quantico ), a Syrian doctor with battle-tested skills in emergency medicine who fled his country with his younger sister, Amira (Sirena Gulamgaus). Together they struggled to build a new life in Canada while Bash strived to rebuild his career in medicine. Transplant was produced by Sphère Média Plus, in association with CTV and NBCUniversal International Studios. “I am beyond grateful and thrilled to partner with this incredible company. I have huge admiration for Netflix’s entire team, and for their unsurpassed drive to tell great stories and connect with audiences around the world,” Kay said in a statement on Wednesday. His TV writing credits include Ransom, This Life and Republic of Doyle. “Joe is a seasoned and gifted creator and showrunner, who is also adept at supporting other writers. We have loved working with him on our shows so far and we are thrilled to expand our relationship,” Danielle Woodrow and Tara Woodbury, directors of content at Netflix Canada, said in their own statement. Kay is represented by Dustin Alpern and Conrad Sun at Sundust Management. The overall deal was negotiated by Casey Chisick of Cassels Brock & Blackwell LLP. THR

The film, which stars Astrit Kabashi, Flonja Kodheli, Kumrije Hoxa, Fiona Gllavica and Alban Ukaj, was co-written by Morina with Doruntina Basha. title: Jennifer Lawrence Says Playing Katniss Again After 11 Years in ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Was ‘Crazy,’ ‘Unbelievable’ and ‘So Beautiful’
full_text: × Oct 28, 2026 6:38am PT Jennifer Lawrence Says Playing Katniss Again After 11 Years in ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Was ‘Crazy,’ ‘Unbelievable’ and ‘So Beautiful’ By Zack Sharf Plus Icon Zack Sharf Digital News Director ZSharf Latest Jennifer Lawrence Says Playing Katniss Again After 11 Years in ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Was ‘Crazy,’ ‘Unbelievable’ and ‘So Beautiful’ 2 hours ago Barry Keoghan Undergoes Skin-Tightening Cosmetic Treatment in Video Posted Months After He Called Out Online Abuse Over ‘How I Look’ 17 hours ago Jennifer Lawrence Did Not Start Her Beauty Brand Because of Hollywood Instability: ‘A Smarter Exit Plan Would Be Signing Up for a Big Franchise’ 22 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source ©Lions Gate/Courtesy Everett Collection Jennifer Lawrence appeared on the latest episode of the “Call Her Daddy” podcast and spoke out for the first time about what it was like to reprise Katniss Everdeen for the first time in 11 years. The Oscar winner is back as her iconic “Hunger Games” character in the upcoming prequel movie “Sunrise on the Reaping,” in theaters Nov. 20 from Lionsgate. “It was unbelievable,” Lawrence said about reprising Katniss. “It was so crazy. It was the same crew. It was the same AD, who I’ve worked with a million times because I love him. And with Josh [Hutcherson] and Woody [Harrelson] … it was so emotional. Josh and I didn’t walk to the bathroom without our arms around each other. It was so beautiful. And Woody, obviously, came through the window of my hotel room uninvited. It wouldn’t be the same if he listened to boundaries or used a door.” Related Stories Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’ Variety reported last December that Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson were returning as Katniss and Peeta Mellark for a scene in “Sunrise on the Reaping.” Lawrence has now let it slip that Woody Harrelson will also be back as Haymitch. The new prequel movie centers on a young Haymitch (played by Joseph Zada) as he competes in the 50th Hunger Games. Book readers know that Suzanne Collins’ “Sunrise on the Reaping” novel ends with a flash-forward epilogue featuring Katniss, Peeta and Haymitch, so it appears the film adpatation is following suit. Lawrence told Variety during her “No Hard Feelings” press tour in 2023 that she was “totally” open to reprising her “Hunger Games” role of Katniss Everdeen should the right opportunity arise. She added at the time, “If Katniss ever could ever come back into my life, 100 percent.” As Katniss, Lawrence headlined four “Hunger Games” movies between 2012 and 2015. The franchise (which also includes the Rachel Zegler-led 2023 prequel “The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes”) has grossed $3.3 billion to date at the worldwide box office. “What made me nervous was how it could negatively affect my acting career and my personal life,” Lawrence said on the “Call Her Daddy” podcast about her biggest concern with joining the franchise when she was 20 years old. “The one thing I was always sure of when I was younger was that I wanted to be a mom, and this looked so different then doing some indies. ‘Twilight’ had just come out and everybody saw what that was. It was more like… how is this going to change my life and my acting career?” Watch Lawrence’s full interview on the “Call Her Daddy” podcast in the video below. title: Peter Medak Dies: ‘The Ruling Class’ & ‘Romeo Is Bleeding’ Director Was 88
full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Peter Medak Dies: ‘The Ruling Class’ & ‘Romeo Is Bleeding’ Director Was 88 Kevin Bleyer Dies: Emmy Winning ‘Daily Show’ Writer & Barack Obama Speech Writer Dies In Car Crash At 54 Broadway’s ‘A Few Good Men’, ‘Other Desert Cities’, ‘860’ Fill Seats With Brisk Autumn Box Office View All October 28, 2026 6:24am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Peter Medak Courtesy Peter Medak , the award-winning Hungarian-British film and television director with a career spanning six decades and credits including The Changeling starring George C. Scott, Romeo Is Bleeding with Gary Oldman and The Krays starring Martin and Gary Kemp, died Tuesday, October 27 in Los Angeles. He was 88. His death was announced by family. Though a cause was not stated, the family noted that Medak died peacefully. Born in Budapest, Hungary in 1937, Medak showed interest in movie-making by the time he was eight years old when his aunt gave him a 35-millimeter hand-cranked projector and a piece of film. At 13, under the Communist regime, he was banned from going to school, later saying, “my father was a so-called capitalist…he was… put away to prison for years. … I spent an awful lot of time on my own, in our apartment, because my father was in prison, my mother was working in a plastics factory, I had a brother who died. …I became an observer… you know, looking through this incredible keyhole of our apartment.” Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries News Kevin Bleyer Dies: Emmy Winning ‘Daily Show’ Writer & Barack Obama Speech Writer Dies In Car Crash At 54 After fleeing to England in 1956 at 18, Medak started as a trainee at Associated British-Pathe, and worked on the sets of major British productions while soon getting promoted to assistant director on films such as The Great Armored Car Swindle (1961) and The Phantom of the Opera (1962). MCA Universal Pictures quickly noticed his work and in 1963, and he was brought to Los Angeles and signed to a television-directing contract, working on the series Court Martial. Watch on Deadline In 1967 Paramount signed him to direct his first feature, Negatives , with Glenda Jackson. His next two films were the highly acclaimed black comedies A Day in the Death of Joe Egg (1972), starring Alan Bates, and The Ruling Class (1972), with Peter O’ Toole, for which Medak was nominated for the Palme D’Or, and O’Toole was nominated for an Academy Award. Medak earned a reputation across his six-decade career as an “actors’ director,” resulting in 27 features with such acclaimed films as The Changeling (1980) with George C. Scott; The Krays (1990); Let Him Have It (1991), and Romeo is Bleeding (1993), with Gary Oldman. His 2018 documentary The Ghost of Peter Sellers received acclaim, winning Best Documentary at the Beverly Hills Film Festival. His prolific television directing work included of Homicide: Life on the Street, Chicago Hope, The Wire and Breaking Bad . With a deep interest in music, he directed some of the earliest music videos for artists such as Peter Gabriel and Pink Floyd, and, in the opera realm, directed La voix humaine with Julia Migenes. He staged a production of Salome in Minneapolis and Rigoletto with the Los Angeles Opera. In a career spanning 60 years, making both cult and critically acclaimed movies, Medak directed 27 features and 59 episodes of television. “If it’s in your blood, directing,” he said once. “You never stop directing and it doesn’t matter that you’re alone in your mind, dreaming or imagining things but you’re always making a movie.” Medak is survived by his children Christopher, Joshua, Karen and Cornelia Medak and grandchildren Sacha, Marlowe, Ryden, Oliver and Anders. He was previously married to Katherine La Kermance, Carolyn Seymour and Julia Migenes, and was in a relationship with Christine Wagner. title: BBC “Disappointed” As Staff Plan Industrial Action Vote Over Job Cuts
full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Russell Brand Forcefully Denies Charges As He Gives Evidence During Rape Trial: “Consent Is More Important Than Sex Itself” Inside The BBC Cuts: Painful Service Closures Begin, But Worse Could Be To Come Meghan Markle “Deeply Distressed” Over Allegation Her Father Possessed Child Abuse Images View All October 28, 2026 6:23am Add us as a Google Preferred Source BBC News presenter Clive Myrie BBC EXCLUSIVE : The BBC ‘s plan to cut more than 100 journalism roles will be put to an industrial ballot amid unrest over the UK broadcaster’s £500 million ($664M) savings strategy. The National Union of Journalists (NUJ) will ballot members next month over newsroom redundancies, with members voting on whether to take strike action or other industrial measures, such as work to rule. BBC News announced last week that the division will close more than 100 roles over the coming months, saving £5.5M. BBC News still needs to find at least another £20M to hit its minimum goal of £51M in savings. Related Stories News BBC Pays $530,000 To 'Mr. Nobody Against Putin' Exec Over Antisemitism Claims News Disney+ Among Buyers For RTÉ & BBC Drama 'The Walsh Sisters' Rhodri Talfan Davies, the BBC’s deputy director general, emailed staff about the NUJ’s decision on Wednesday, saying the ballot was a “disappointing development.” Watch on Deadline “Over recent months, we have had extensive and constructive discussions with the NUJ and been clear that we will do everything possible to minimise compulsory redundancies. We’ve backed that up with action too – a large majority of the redundancies agreed to date have been achieved on a voluntary basis,” Talfan Davies said. “Faced with a £500 million financial savings challenge and significant operational pressures, we cannot offer a guarantee that there will be no compulsory redundancies. Whilst we will continue to do everything possible to minimise this, the reality is that no organisation of our scale and complexity could offer such an undertaking and it would inevitably compromise our service to audiences if we did.” The NUJ ballot will run from November 3 to 24. It is separate from a second ballot on pay, which closes on November 5. The BBC has increased its pay offer to a 1.5% rise or a minimum of £1,000, depending on which is higher. The corporation previously offered a 1% rise or a minimum of £500. The BBC has also ditched controversial changes to staff terms, including slashing usage for night shift workers . The NUJ and Bectu have a neutral position on the BBC pay offer, meaning they have neither endorsed nor denounced the deal. title: Comedy Legend George Schlatter Sets Doc Release With Freestyle Digital Media (Exclusive)
full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 28, 2026 6:05am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Producer George Schlatter made an appearance at the Newport Beach Film Festival premiere of his doc 'Sock It to Me: The Legend of George Schlatter.' Tiffany Rose/Getty Images for Newport Beach Film Festival Freestyle Digital Media, the digital film distribution division of Byron Allen ’s Allen Media Group, has picked up the North American VOD rights to Sock It To Me: The Legend of George Schlatter . The feature documentary about Schlatter, the creator of Rowan & Martin’s Laugh-In , the groundbreaking comedy variety hour that launched on NBC in 1968, will debut on digital platforms from Dec. 8. Laugh In launched the careers of Goldie Hawn and Lily Tomlin and gave birth to late-night television, including Saturday Night Live. Schlatter also created and produced the NBC reality series Real People from 1979 that featured an 18 year-old Byron Allen in his first TV gig as a regular co-host. Recalling a seven-decade career as a prolific TV producer and director, Sock It To Me uses archival footage and interviews with stars like Hawn, Tom Hanks, Tomlin, Martin Short, Billy Crystal, Jay Leno, Jimmy Kimmel, Lionel Richie, Lisa Ann Walter, Berry Gordy and Byron Allen to explore how Schlatter, now 96, changed TV comedy. “People have been asking me to write an autobiography, and I’ve always said have somebody else write it. They then explained to me that it wouldn’t be an autobiography, so here we are,” Schlatter said in a statement. “It’s a full circle moment to work with Byron Allen’s company to get this documentary out into the world. You bet your sweet bippy I’m excited for audiences to see it and remind them of the power of laughter!” Written and directed by Chris Coronado, Sock It To Me was produced by Coronado, Greg Myers and Dayna Winston. Since 2016, Coronado has served as creative director at George Schlatter Productions, overseeing the creative development and production of documentary and entertainment projects. Freestyle Digital Media negotiated the deal to acquire Sock It To Me directly with the filmmakers and George Schlatter Productions. THR

title: Annecy Title ‘Cloud Girl’ Flies To International Buyers For SC Films

The feature from French writer-director Philippe Riche was inspired by Romain Puértolas’ 2015 novel The Little Girl Who Swallowed a Cloud as Big as the Eiffel Tower and screened as an Official Selection of the 2026 Annecy International Animation Film Festival. Viva Pictures will release the film in U.S. cinemas on January 8, 2027. Pan Distribution has taken rights for France, Pathé Films for French-Speaking Switzerland and O’Brother for Benelux.
